title: Cortical Desynchronization and Autonomic Reactivity under Acute Cognitive Stress
authors: Dr. Sarah Lin, Dr. Marcus Vance, Elena Rostova
abstract: We investigated the temporal coupling between EEG frequency shifts (alpha/beta ratio) and electrodermal responses (GSR) in 45 participants subjected to the Stroop task. Results show a significant correlation between prefrontal beta power increases and skin conductance response amplitude, indicating coupled central and autonomic nervous system mobilization under acute stressors.

title: Heart Rate Variability (HRV) as a Predictor of Emotional Regulation Capacity in Virtual Reality
authors: Dr. Marcus Vance, David K. Park
abstract: This study evaluated high-frequency HRV (HF-HRV) in immersive virtual environments designed to elicit fear or relaxation. Participants with higher baseline RMSSD (root mean square of successive differences) exhibited faster physiological recovery rates when transitioning from stress-inducing virtual environments to soothing natural settings.

title: Visual Attention and Pupil Dilatory Dynamics in Adaptive User Interfaces
abstract: Using a Tobii Pro Spectrum 1200Hz eye tracker, we monitored gaze fixation and pupil dilation in designers performing complex layout optimization. Pupil dilation rate accurately indexed cognitive overload points, presenting a viable metric for adaptive UI interfaces that dynamically scale information density.

title: Prefrontal Hemodynamic Activity and Alpha Power Coherence During Mindful Breathing Practices
authors: Prof. T. Takahashi, Dr. Sarah Lin, Kenji Sato
abstract: We utilized a combined EEG-fNIRS configuration to measure neural correlates of focused attention meditation. Mindful breathing led to increased prefrontal oxygenated hemoglobin concentration alongside enhanced parieto-occipital alpha band coherence, validating biofeedback training efficacy for attention control.

title: Sympathetic Nervous Arousal and Visual Gaze Patterns in High-Arousal Phobic Stimuli
authors: David K. Park, Elena Rostova, Dr. Marcus Vance
abstract: By exposing arachnophobic individuals to virtual spiders, we tracked the temporal sequence of visual avoidance and skin conductance spikes. Eye-tracking fixation duration on phobic objects preceded GSR rises by 1.2 seconds, supporting the hypothesis of hyper-vigilant cognitive processing prior to autonomic output.
